brief.subject: Diesel jumps 9.7 cents; contract rates hold above 10%
brief.headline: Diesel Climbs to $6.276 as Truckload Contract Rate Gains Stay Above 10%
brief.dek: Diesel rose 9.7 cents last week, contract rate increases keep running hot, and cost pressure hits reefer carrier Marten.
brief.lede: Diesel averaged $6.276 per gallon in the week of 2026-10-19, up 9.7 cents from the prior week. That reverses part of a four-week slide and squeezes margins again.

sections.heading: Diesel Bounces Back Up
bullets: $6.276 per gallon: EIA's U.S. retail diesel average for the week of 2026-10-19.
Up 9.7 cents (1.6%) week over week, a sharp hit to per-mile fuel costs.
Still down 25.3 cents over four weeks, so recent relief has only partly eroded.
A first Russian diesel shipment is heading to the U.S. after a Trump-Putin deal; any pump impact is unclear.

sections.heading: Contract Rate Hikes Stay Strong
bullets: Above 10%: truckload contract rate increases are holding steady, per a new SONAR index.
Carriers are landing increases roughly equal to several years' worth in one cycle.
Small fleets renewing lanes now have firmer ground to push for higher rates.

sections.heading: Costs Bite a Reefer Carrier
bullets: 7%: Marten Transport shares fell after a weak third quarter.
Rising fuel and health insurance costs outweighed better supply-demand conditions.
Small reefer operators face the same cost squeeze even as the market tightens.

sections.heading: Cross-Border Shifts
bullets: Oct. 30: plywood and some packaging materials drop off the 50% Canada tariff list, while other goods are added.
Roadrunner launches Canada-to-U.S. LTL service with a 5.9% general rate increase effective Nov. 2.
$641M: avocado imports' value to U.S. trucking and warehousing, supporting Texas border freight.

sections.heading: Freight Demand Signals
bullets: Drewry's World Container Index rose on trans-Pacific gains, pointing to firmer import demand.
More than $1.6B: five shippers' new or expanded U.S. plants, including trailer and bus production.
Nestlé will close an Ohio factory by end of 2027, shifting production to South Carolina.
